the generation of a spoken dialogue system that can be used to interact with the users in a natural way.
the development of a new NLG model for spoken dialogue systems that can be trained from scratch and can be easily adapted to new domains and tasks.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed NLG generator can be trained to learn from multi-domain datasets, and it can generalize to unseen domains.
we have successfully integrated a novel encoder-decoder based architecture with an attention mechanism into the spoken dialogue system to generate the required sentences.

we propose a novel RNN Encoder Decoder architecture for NLG, which can be trained jointly for sentence planning and surface realisation and can be used to generate natural language sentences in a spoken dialogue systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the encoder-decoder framework is very effective for the task of natural language generation and it has the potential to be a strong alternative to the traditional rule-based approaches.
the RNN based Encoder Decoder architecture with the attention mechanism can serve as a strong baseline model for spoken dialogue systems.
a single generator can be used for all the domains, which makes it easy for a spoken dialogue system designer to integrate the NLG component into their system.
